evidence.claim: RMF API schemas require task category/description and separate request success, dispatch state and ongoing task status; requester is an optional string, not proof of enterprise authorization.
evidence.locator: task_request properties/required; dispatch_task_response oneOf; task_state $defs.status and $defs.dispatch
evidence.limitations: Schema establishes message semantics, not deployment authorization or physical success. Component release pin is not a tested compatible full stack.

evidence.claim: RMF dispatcher validates requests, queues bidding then responds success; bounded in-process response cache uses request IDs; lingering dispatch commands expire after 10 s. Dispatched work becomes fleet-adapter responsibility.
evidence.limitations: Acceptance is not assignment/completion. Cache is bounded process memory, not durable enterprise idempotency. Actual deployment settings, behavior under load and installed version unverified.

evidence.claim: RMF fleet callbacks admit feasible supported requests; EasyFullControl integrates navigation/stop/action callbacks, with integrator-provided completion and activity feedback. Defaults differ between API layers.
evidence.locator: EasyFullControl lines 50–53; RobotCallbacks 337–375; CommandExecution 378–426; FleetUpdateHandle consider_delivery/cleaning/patrol/composed callbacks
evidence.limitations: Header contract does not establish site installation or correct operator authorization. No LLM coordination gain or safety-certified behavior inferred.

evidence.claim: Fleet TaskManager validates cancellation then replies success if cancel_task accepts; active-task cancellation calls cancel and returns rather than waiting for physical stop or business rollback. When cancel_task returns false, this handler sends no success response and does not emit an explicit negative reply there.
evidence.limitations: Cancellation acknowledgement does not establish completed cancellation/physical stop. No assessment of emergency-stop safety or all phase-specific cancellation code. No-response and caller timeout must not be treated as proof that the task is absent or physically stopped.

evidence.claim: rmf-web task route persists RMF task state/request after successful dispatch; bridge generates fresh UUID per call and defaults to 5 s response timeout. Repeated HTTP call therefore has a new ROS identity in this implementation.
evidence.limitations: Timeout-after-acceptance duplicate effect is a code-derived hypothesis, not observed incident. User dependency exists; target deployment auth/policy unverified. Distinct older web release not asserted compatible with newer core/schema pins.
